title: JBMC's two readings on the five recorded JBMC examples job -073804 could not run (128-131, 134), now with their patches applied
description: Job 20261106-073804 read every JBMC run of the 41 recorded JBMC examples both through --json-ui and as text: 78 runs, 0 disagreements. Examples 128-131 and 134 gave no verdict there, because their git-format patches were never applied in the job's work directory (git apply inside this repository's tree skipped every file; fixed in commit 'Pipeline jobs apply git-format patches'). This job runs those five with JVMCONTRACT_JBMC_READ=both, on copies of examples/ so nothing recorded changes. A pass means both readings agree on every run and each example gives its recorded verdict, which completes the differential: the text reader can then be removed (step 4b of the sound-verdicts brief).
expected: exits 0; every JBMC run of 128-131 and 134 read alike both ways, and each example's verdict as recorded

resources.notes: the five took seconds each when recorded; 134 ran 1049 s in -073804 only because it ran unpatched; -073804 peaked at 1.4 GiB

steps.name: 5 recorded JBMC examples, read both ways
steps.run:
set -eo pipefail
W=lib/target/jobs/4b-differential-5; rm -rf "$W"; mkdir -p "$W/repo"
cp -r examples "$W/repo/"
(cd lib && cargo build --release -q)
export JVMCONTRACT="$PWD/lib/target/release/jvmcontract" JVMCONTRACT_JBMC_READ=both JVMCONTRACT_JBMC_DIFFERENTIAL="$PWD/$W/differential.jsonl"
status=0; python3 "$W/repo/examples/tools/build.py" 128 129 130 131 134 > "$W/build.txt" 2>&1 || status=$?
tail -8 "$W/build.txt"
python3 - "$W/differential.jsonl" "$status" <<'PY'
import json, sys
lines = [json.loads(l) for l in open(sys.argv[1])]
bad = [d for d in lines if not d["agree"]]
endings = {}
for d in lines:
    endings[d["json"]["ending"]] = endings.get(d["json"]["ending"], 0) + 1
print(f"{len(lines)} JBMC runs read both ways, {len(bad)} disagreeing; endings from the JSON: {endings}")
for d in bad:
    print("DISAGREE", d["log"], d["stage"], d["differences"])
assert lines, "no JBMC run was read both ways"
assert not bad, "the readings disagree"
assert sys.argv[2] == "0", f"build.py exited {sys.argv[2]}: a verdict differs from its expected one (see build.txt)"
print("ok: the JSON and the text reading agree on every run of the five examples, and every verdict is as expected")
PY
